You are working in the Go repository checked out at /gin (github.com/gin-gonic/gin v1.8.1, a web framework). The repository has had a BUG deliberately injected into the source file /gin/response_writer.go (a single small semantic mutation of the original upstream code, e.g. a changed operator, constant, comparison, receiver, or swapped expression). Your job: find that injected bug in /gin/response_writer.go and fix it with a minimal edit so that a hidden test named `TestResponseWriterStatusCode` (which is NOT present in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour, i.e. the status-code behaviour of the responseWriter) would pass.

Method hints: read /gin/response_writer.go and /gin/response_writer_test.go carefully. Compare the code against its own comments and against the documented behaviour of gin's ResponseWriter interface (Status() returns the HTTP response status code of the current request, Size() bytes written, Written() true once body written, WriteHeaderNow() forces the header write). Look for any line that is subtly wrong, e.g. a comparison that should be different, a constant that should be different (noWritten = -1, defaultStatus = http.StatusOK), an assignment that should be a different field, a missing/incorrect guard, or a receiver/return mistake. Write small temporary Go test files (package gin) in /gin to probe behaviour empirically (e.g. call writer.reset(httptest.NewRecorder()), WriteHeader(300), WriteHeaderNow(), then check w.Status() and the recorder's Code; try WriteHeader(0); try Write then WriteHeader; try Status() before/after WriteHeaderNow) and DELETE any temporary test files you create before finishing.

Hard constraints: do NOT modify any *_test.go file that already exists in the repo; do NOT break any existing test (`cd /gin && go test ./...` must pass, and it currently passes 100%). Do not make unrelated changes or add features. When done, report: the exact diff you applied (git diff), the reasoning for why it is the injected bug, and the output of `cd /gin && go test ./...`.
